title: OPPO Reno 16 Price Hiked by Up to Rs 7,000 in India, Top Model Now Rs 79,999
excerpt: The Reno 16's second price increase since launch takes the 8GB model to Rs 72,999 and the 12GB model to Rs 79,999 — Rs 11,000-12,000 above launch prices. A new 8GB/128GB variant at Rs 65,999 is now the entry point.
body:
• OPPO has raised the Reno 16's India price by up to Rs 7,000, effective October 22: the 8GB/256GB model now costs Rs 72,999 and the 12GB/256GB model Rs 79,999.
  • It is the phone's second hike. Prices rose Rs 5,000 in August, so both models now cost Rs 11,000-12,000 more than at launch.
  • A new 8GB RAM / 128GB storage variant at Rs 65,999 is now the cheapest Reno 16.
  • Before you buy: at Rs 79,999 the top Reno 16 — a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 phone — sits in flagship territory, so compare it against discounted flagships before paying the new price.

OPPO has increased the price of the Reno 16 in India by up to Rs 7,000, with the revised prices reflected on the company's official India website, Gadgets 360 reported after verifying the listings. The change was first flagged by tipster Sanju Choudhary on X.

The New Prices

The 8GB RAM and 256GB storage variant has gone from Rs 66,999 to Rs 72,999, a Rs 6,000 increase, and the 12GB/256GB configuration from Rs 72,999 to Rs 79,999, up Rs 7,000. OPPO has also introduced an 8GB/128GB variant priced at Rs 65,999, which becomes the entry point to the range.

The Reno 16 launched earlier this year at Rs 61,999 and Rs 67,999 for the two original configurations. A Rs 5,000 hike followed in August. Against launch prices, buyers now pay Rs 11,000 more for the 8GB model and Rs 12,000 more for the 12GB model — for identical hardware.

Why Prices Keep Rising

OPPO has not publicly explained this revision. Reporting across the industry ties the wave of smartphone price increases to rising memory costs, as demand for DRAM from AI data centres tightens supply. 91Mobiles noted that almost every new and older phone line is going through the same shift, and OPPO's own Reno 16c and A-series phones have seen earlier increases of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000.

What You Get, and the Competition

The Reno 16 is a premium mid-range phone: a compact 6.32-inch 1.5K 120Hz AMOLED display, a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 processor, triple 50-megapixel rear cameras, a 6,700mAh battery and 80W fast charging. At its old prices, that package competed with premium mid-rangers. At Rs 79,999, the 12GB model is priced against discounted flagships, and against performance-focused rivals such as the iQOO 15R and OnePlus 15R that cost less.

The practical advice is unchanged by the branding: if the Reno 16's design and cameras are your priority, the new 128GB variant at Rs 65,999 is the value pick in the range. If you were about to pay Rs 79,999 for the 12GB model, price-check flagship alternatives first — the gap the Reno line used to exploit has largely closed.

The hardware itself is unchanged by the revision. The Reno 16 carries a triple 50-megapixel rear system — a main camera, a 116-degree ultra-wide and a periscope telephoto with 3.5x optical zoom and optical image stabilisation — plus a 50-megapixel front camera, 4K video at 60fps on both sides, IP66, IP68 and IP69 dust and water ratings, and Android 16-based ColorOS 16. It is 8.22mm thick in its violet and purple finishes.

That specification is why the new pricing stings: at Rs 79,999, the 12GB Reno 16 now sits alongside OPPO's own Find X9, listed at Rs 77,995, and sale pricing on Apple's iPhone 16, while bank offers routinely pull full flagships into the same bracket. Buyers are no longer choosing between a mid-ranger and a flagship — at this price, they are choosing between two flagships, one of which has a mid-range processor.
